# Fixtures for `tests/no-grep-q-under-pipefail.sh`

`--self-test` scans this directory and compares its findings with the lines marked `# EXPECT` (a marker on a comment-only line does not count). Every marked line must be reported exactly once, and nothing else may be.

- `positive/shapes.sh` sets pipefail and holds one spelling of `producer | grep -q` per line: `egrep`, `fgrep`, `--quiet`, `--silent`, `-q` inside a flag cluster, `-q` after the pattern, a trailing `|` or a backslash with grep on the next line, `|&`, a `#` inside a quoted string before the pipe, a trailing comment that quotes the idiom, `command grep` and a path to grep.
- `positive/prefixes.sh` sets pipefail and holds what runs grep without being grep (an assignment, `env`, `env -u NAME`, `timeout N`, `timeout -s SIG N`, `command -p`), the other early-exit options (`-qm1`, `-m1`, `--max-count=1`, `-l`, `-L`), and three lines that must not hide the rest of the file from the scan: an arithmetic shift `$((1 << SHIFT))`, an arithmetic `<<=`, and a here-string of a bare word (`<<<word`), each followed by a reported line.
- `positive/substitutions.sh` sets pipefail and holds pipelines inside command substitutions: `"$(...)"`, `$(...)`, backticks inside double quotes, two lines inside a multi-line `$(for ...)` (each reported at its own line), and a `"$(...)"` on a quoted string's second line (reported at the line the statement starts).
- `positive/prefixes.sh` also holds `nice -n N`, `stdbuf`, `time` and `sudo -u USER` before grep, a backslashed (`\grep`) and a quoted (`"grep"`) command name, a brace group (`{ grep -q a; }`), both `--files-with-matches` and `--files-without-match`, and abbreviated long options (`--qui`, `--max-c=1`, and `--files-with`, a prefix of two early options). `positive/exec-in-pipe.sh` reads the pipe with `exec grep -q`; `positive/shebang-env-s.sh` sets pipefail only on its interpreter line (`#!/usr/bin/env -S bash -eo pipefail`).
- `sourced-subst/tests/runner.sh` sets pipefail and sources `"$(dirname "$0")/../helpers/by-dirname.sh"` and `"$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/../helpers/by-cd.sh"`: command substitutions with quotes of their own. Both helpers are reported.
- `positive/lexer-edges.sh` holds lines that must not hide the rest of the file (a here-document word escaped with a backslash, `<<\EOF`; a word with hyphens, `<<END-OF-TEXT`; an ANSI-C string with an escaped quote, `$'it\'s'`; a plain here-document whose body holds an indented copy of its word), each followed by a reported line, then `| if grep -q` and the three-character abbreviations `--q`, `--s` and `--m`.
- `positive/set-separate.sh` (`set -e -o pipefail`), `positive/set-long.sh` (`set -o errexit -o nounset -o pipefail`) and `positive/shopt.sh` (`shopt -so pipefail`): each is in scope, and its one pipeline is reported.
- `lib/helper.sh` sets nothing but lives under `lib/`, whose files are sourced into scripts that set pipefail: reported.
- `sourced/runner.sh` sets pipefail and sources `sourced/util.sh`, which sets nothing and is not under `lib/`: the helper's pipeline is reported (a sourced file runs with its caller's options), the runner's own here-string is not.
- `sourced-var/tests/runner.sh` sets pipefail and sources `"$PLUGIN_DIR/helpers/util.sh"`, where `PLUGIN_DIR` is the directory above it; `sourced-var/tests/runner-by-name.sh` sources `"$HELPER_PATH"`, a variable it assigns one path. The helpers set nothing and are not under `lib/`; each one's pipeline is reported.
- `control/safe-forms.sh` sets pipefail and holds only shapes that are safe or not pipelines: here-strings, a file argument, `grep` without `-q` to `/dev/null`, `grep -c`, a `|` inside a quoted pattern, `||`, comments quoting the idiom, a here-document body, a pipeline inside a `bash -c` string and one inside a double-quoted `ssh` argument (another shell, which does not inherit `set -o pipefail`), and a reads-to-end grep inside `"$(...)"`. Nothing is reported.
- `control/no-pipefail.sh` holds the idiom but never sets pipefail, so the pipeline's status is grep's own: not reported.
- `control/grep-args.sh` sets pipefail and holds a q that is not an option: `grep -eq` (the pattern "q"), `grep -e -q`, `grep --regexp -q`, `grep --regex=-q` (an abbreviation of an option with an argument), `grep -- -q`, plus `-A1`, `--fi=` (an abbreviation that is not an early option), `--co` (ambiguous among `--color`, `--colour`, `--context` and `--count`) and prefixed greps without an early-exit option. Nothing is reported.
- `control/shopt-unset.sh` turns pipefail off with `shopt -uo pipefail` and prints the words `set -o pipefail` with `echo`: not in scope, not reported.
- `control/helpers/util.sh` has the same relative path as `sourced-var/helpers/util.sh`, is sourced by nothing and sets nothing: not reported, so the runner's `$PLUGIN_DIR/helpers/util.sh` is resolved from the runner's own directories, not by the path's tail.
